public_rationale: Marcus said the massive Behemoth model 'so far isn't working.' Read plainly, that means it was not performing well enough to meet Meta's goals or be released. Two days before the post, the WSJ reported that Meta delayed Behemoth after engineers struggled to substantially improve its capabilities. It also reported that executives blamed the Llama 4 team for 'the failure to make progress on Behemoth.' In April, Meta said Behemoth beat some rival models on certain STEM benchmarks. But Meta also said it was still training and not released, and the later reporting says this performance did not hold up internally. A July NYT report adds that the release was held back over poor internal performance. On the ordinary reading, the claim holds. It would not hold if 'isn't working' meant the model literally did not function.
limitations: The result depends on reading 'isn't working' as 'not meeting its goals,' not as 'non-functional.'
The key reporting relies on anonymous sources. Meta did not confirm the reasons for the delay.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The massive Behemoth model has so far not been working.

statement.excerpt: Funny name - Behemoth - for absolutely massive model that so far isn’t working.

our_interpretation: Behemoth is Meta's Llama 4 Behemoth, a model with about 2 trillion parameters that Meta previewed on 2025-04-05.
Plain reading of 'isn't working': so far the model has not performed well enough to meet Meta's goals or be released. It does not mean the model literally fails to run.
Target period: from Meta's preview (2025-04-05) to the post date (2025-05-17).
criteria.support_condition: Credible reports from the period say Meta held back or delayed Behemoth because its performance or progress fell short of expectations.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Behemoth was released, or credible reports in the period say it was meeting its goals and on track, with no performance problems behind any delay.

evidence.excerpt: Meta had completed training its Behemoth model by feeding in data to improve it, but delayed its release due to poor internal performance.
